name: Excalibur, Sword of Eden
blocked_sentences: This spell costs {X} less to cast, where X is the total mana value of historic permanents you control. (Artifacts, legendaries, and Sagas are historic.)

needs.what: a fifth cost-reduction shape, `total_mana_value: {filter}`, that SUMS the mana values of every permanent its filter matches, alongside the existing `count`, `total_power` and `greatest_mana_value` -- the mana-value analogue of `total_power`, read by `reduction_amount` in src/automtg/engine/cost_reduction.py and admitted to `COST_REDUCTION_KEYS` in src/automtg/cards/loader/vocabulary.py
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `cost_reduction` takes exactly one of `count`, `total_power`, `amount`, `greatest_mana_value`. `greatest_mana_value` reads mana values but takes a MAXIMUM, and its own docstring says it is a separate key precisely because it must not sum -- two permanents of mana value 3 and 5 give 5, not 8. `total_power` sums, but sums power, which an Equipment-and-Saga board mostly has none of (a Saga and a Signet are power 0, yet mana value 3 and 2). `count` gives 1 per permanent, and `amount` is a flat number needing a condition. The effect-value language already sums mana values -- `mana_value_of` with an `objects` ref, used by Phoenix's "total mana value of other permanents you control" -- but that language is `value_keys`, unreachable from a `cost_reduction` spec, which the loader restricts to `COST_REDUCTION_KEYS`.

needs.what: an or-of-characteristics filter inside a cost reduction -- `any_of` (as the effect-side selector language already has) or a `historic: true` key -- so a reduction can count permanents that are Artifact OR Legendary OR Saga, i.e. a disjunction across types, supertypes and subtypes at once
needs.why_existing_wont_do: A cost-reduction filter may use `STATIC_FILTER_KEYS` plus `zone` (COST_REDUCTION_FILTER_KEYS), and `_reduction_matches` ANDs every key it reads: `{"types":["Artifact"],"supertypes":["Legendary"],"subtypes":["Saga"]}` matches only a permanent that is all three at once, which nothing is. `any_types` is the closest listed key, but it is an or over TYPES only (`set(any_types) & card.types`) and Legendary is a supertype and Saga a subtype, so it cannot reach either half; it is also not read by `_reduction_matches` at all today. `any_of` is how the shipped pool spells historic -- Lost to Legend's target selector in data/cards/auto/templates.cards.json is exactly `any_of: [{types:[Artifact]}, {supertypes:[Legendary]}, {subtypes:[Saga]}]` -- but `any_of` is a `selector_keys` entry, not a static or reduction filter key, so the loader rejects it here.
